verdict.line: You lose if you facecheck Rupture poke before level 6; you win if you stack Siphoning Strike safely and let a finished Trinity Force carry the mid-late all-ins.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath wins the early poke war with Rupture's 950-range skillshot and Feral Scream's silence while Nasus is stuck farming at 255 range, which is why Cho'Gath holds lane and solo-kill advantage. The 50% head-to-head over 190 games exists because Nasus's Siphoning Strike stacks and Soul Eater lifesteal scale harder than Cho'Gath's flat burst once levels and items catch up.

theirWindow.when: after he lands Rupture on you
theirWindow.what: He follows the pop-up and slow with Feral Scream's silence and free Vorpal Spikes autos. You can't Wither or Spirit Fire back during the silence, so just walk out of range instead of trading.

yourWindow.what: Drop Spirit Fire first to shred his armor, then commit. Your stacked Siphoning Strike damage plus Soul Eater lifesteal out-trade his Vorpal Spikes, and after level 6 Fury of the Sands turns any skirmish in your favor.

start.why: 66.1% pick rate and the highest winrate start (49.4% over 160 games) — the flat damage reduction and regen let you eat Rupture and Vorpal Spikes chip damage while you farm for Q stacks.

boots.why: Highest-winning boots (53.2% over 109 games, 47.4% pick) — the ability haste lowers Siphoning Strike's cooldown (8/7/6/5/4s) and Wither's (15/14/13/12/11s), letting you stack and peel more often.

core.why: Best-performing completed path (58.8% over 17 games) — the stat stick turns every stacked Siphoning Strike auto into a real damage spike.
Stacks with Soul Eater's lifesteal so your sustain in extended trades scales with both your passive and your stacked Q, not just one.
The attack speed slow from Frozen Heart blunts Cho'Gath's Vorpal Spikes trading and the ability haste keeps Spirit Fire and Wither on a short leash.

runes.keystoneWhy: The movement and heal-on-move help you reposition out of Rupture's landing zone and the attack speed burst lets you proc extra Soul Eater lifesteal when you do get to stack safely.

summoners.why: Highest-winning combo on record (52.8% over fewer games but the top performer) — Nasus has no dash, so Ghost is how you dodge Rupture's 950-range cast and disengage, while Flash is your out against a point-blank Feast execute once he's low on cooldown.

playing.title: Hug minions against Rupture
playing.detail: Cho'Gath's Q (Rupture) is a 950-range ground-targeted spell that pops you up and slows on hit. Stand behind your wave so minions eat it instead of you.

playing.title: Stack, don't trade, pre-6
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike (Q, 255 range, 8/7/6/5/4s cooldown) only grows stronger on kills, so prioritize safely last-hitting over contesting autos until you have a real stack lead.

playing.title: Never cast into an up silence
playing.detail: Feral Scream (W, 300 range cone, 13s cooldown) silences you. If it's up, don't commit Spirit Fire or Fury of the Sands — he'll cancel your follow-up for free.

playing.title: Wither before you commit
playing.detail: You have no gap-closer, so land Wither (W, 700 range, 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown) on him before engaging; it decelerates his movement and attack speed so he can't just kite and spike you with Vorpal Spikes.

playing.title: Shred armor before all-in
playing.detail: Drop Spirit Fire (E, 650 range, 12s cooldown) on him before fighting — the armor reduction plus your lifesteal from Soul Eater swings extended trades toward you.

playing.title: Respect the Feast execute threshold
playing.detail: Feast (R, melee range 175, 60s cooldown) deals high true damage and grows his max health permanently (up to 6 stacks) on a kill. Back off once you're low rather than greeding a trade.

playing.title: Time Fury of the Sands to flip fights
playing.detail: After level 6, Fury of the Sands (R, 120s cooldown, 400 range) drains nearby enemies' max health into bonus damage and boosts your health and range — use it to turn his engage into your all-in, not the reverse.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and winrates above come from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the lane-by-lane tactical reading — when to stack, when to trade, when to disengage — is my own analysis of the ability kits.

stats.opponentTip: It is vital to avoid Cho’Gath’s (Q). Focus on avoiding enemy abilities while keeping your [Q] stacks up, and try to look for an opportunity after reaching level 6. Pay attention to managing your health.
